prompts.contribution: Use case: illustration-story. Create a thoughtful professional hand-drawn technology textbook illustration about improving an open-source learning guide after another person tries reading it. Landscape 3:2, 1536x1024. Scene: an intimate university library alcove, seen at standing eye level in a close three-quarter composition, NOT an overhead desk. Two adult university students collaborate beside a waist-high reading lectern. The reader on the left points to a confusing step on an unfolded short printed guide; the author on the right listens and adds a small corrective insert in coral pencil. Three material layers are visibly distinct: an older guide with a folded corner, a small source card clipped to it, and the newly inserted explanation. A slender shelf of well-used reference binders in the background suggests a shared resource others can continue to improve. The reader is actively testing comprehension, not receiving a trophy or praising a finished product. Realistic recognizable paper, binder clips, pencils, notebook and human gestures; credible anatomy and natural expressions. A little visual wit: the added insert bridges a literal gap between two panels of the foldout guide. Refined graphite and colored-pencil linework, restrained ink hatching, matte gouache on warm ivory uncoated paper #F6F3EB, dark ink #1D2433, indigo #5146D9, teal #3F958D, small coral #F27A59 accents. Plenty of breathing room around the central interaction. No readable lettering, no numerals, no logos, no fake computer UI, no robots, no glowing brain, no neon or ornamental floating network. This is a conceptual publishing illustration, not documentation of an actual classroom trial.

targeted_edit: Edit only the printed guide and its clipped cards in this illustration. Keep the two adult students, faces, hands, library lectern, background, lighting, composition, and pencil/gouache style exactly unchanged. The guide must be about understanding an AI open-source software project, NOT gardening or plant growth. Remove every plant, tree, root, seedling, watering can, soil pile, log and botanical diagram from ALL paper surfaces (including the small source card and the coral correction insert). Replace these paper-only diagrams with restrained hand-sketched document thumbnails, simple file/folder icons, a small laptop outline and a magnifying glass examining a source document; use simple straight arrows to suggest finding a project, reading its source, and checking a guide. On the coral insert, show a newly added explanation as a short row of abstract horizontal lines and one little outlined document, no roots. No readable text, no branded UI or fabricated software screenshot. Background plants, if any, can stay. Preserve all other pixels as much as possible.
